pages.text: Day 77. A star begins as a cloud. I harvest $(fluid)Nebular Gas$() with the Dark Matter Halo Collector and collapse it into a $(item)Protostar$() in the $(item)Nucleosynthesis Chamber$().

Gravity squeezes until the core reaches millions of degrees and hydrogen fuses. I ignite the protostar into a $(item)Stellar Core$(). When a real star runs low on hydrogen its outer layers balloon outward; mine swells into a $(item)Red Giant$(), and I keep its $(item)White Dwarf$() - the bare, glowing core left behind.

White dwarfs forge $(item)Stellar Iron$() - the end of fusion. Iron's nucleus is among the most tightly bound there is; fusing it costs energy instead of releasing it. Dyson shells are made of stellar iron.

A red giant crushed onto stellar iron goes supernova. Its remnant feeds the $(item)r-process$() - rapid neutron capture, nature's way of making gold and everything heavier - and it is needed for every quark star.
A collapsing knot of nebular gas, hot enough to glow but not yet to fuse.$(br2)Made in $(item)Nucleosynthesis Chamber$().
Iron from the core of a star - the end of fusion. Making anything heavier costs energy instead of releasing it.$(br2)Made in $(item)Nucleosynthesis Chamber$().
What is left after a star's core collapses and its outer layers are blasted across the galaxy.$(br2)Made in $(item)Neutron Star Forge$().
A captive star the size of a fist, ignited by a white hole.$(br2)Made in $(item)Stellar Plasma Crucible$().
